results.description:
Dan signec up to the belt and road initiative,behind the back of the federal government.The other countries doing it are in huge debt to China.Tonga and the Pacific nations affect Australiaʼs prosperity.

Heavily Indebted or Defaulting Countries
• Laos: External debt has exceeded 100% to 130% of its GDP Laos | Facebook, driven by large-scale projects like the Boten-Vientiane railway Laos | Facebook and heavy debt owed to Chinese policy banks.
• Sri Lanka: Declared sovereign default in 2022 after external debt outran reserves, leading to a 99-year lease and 70% control stake in the Hambantota Port given to China Merchants in exchange for debt relief.
• Zambia: Defaulted on its external debt in 2020 after China declined initial suspension requests, though debt restructuring talks have since proceeded.
• Pakistan: The largest debtor to China via the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), relying heavily on loan rollovers and refinancing from Beijing.
• Tajikistan: Owing a massive share of its GDP to China, it previously settled a portion of past financial obligations by ceding territory in the Pamir mountain range.
• Tonga & Pacific Nations: Tonga faces repayments to China reaching roughly 25% of its GDP, forcing a heavy reliance on external budgetary assistance from countries like Australia.
• Angola: Heavily indebted through oil-backed loans from the China Development Bank, leading to renegotiations and payment structures tied to oil exports.

results.title: China’s railways carried 3.71 billion passengers in the first three quarters, +4.8% YoY.
results.description:
China’s railways carried 3.71 billion passengers in the first three quarters, +4.8% YoY. Tourist trains rose 25.5%; cross-border travel via Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong HSR and China-Laos Railway grew 11.8% and 37.8%. Foreign passenger trips exceeded 19 million, +33.4%. An ever-denser HSR network brings a surging vitality to a mobile China.
